report_name: Ex-US Soldier 'kiberphant0m' Jailed for Hacking Telecom Giants

threat_actors.name: kiberphant0m
threat_actors.description: A former U.S. Army soldier, Cameron John Wagenius, who conducted a large-scale hacking and extortion campaign against at least 10 U.S. companies, including major telecommunications firms, while on active duty. He also attempted to sell stolen data to a foreign intelligence service.
threat_actors.goals: To extort over $1 million from victim companies by stealing their data and threatening to leak it, and to sell the stolen data to a foreign intelligence service.

attack_patterns.name: Password Guessing
attack_patterns.description: Used a custom tool named 'SSH Brute' to conduct brute-force attacks against SSH servers to gain initial access.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Used stolen legitimate credentials to access corporate systems and cloud environments, including the Snowflake data platform.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Cloud Storage
attack_patterns.description: Exfiltrated hundreds of thousands of sensitive records, including customer PII and call history, from the Snowflake cloud data platform.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Information Repositories
attack_patterns.description: Targeted and exfiltrated data from large databases and cloud storage repositories.

tools.name: SSH Brute
tools.description: A custom tool developed and used by 'kiberphant0m' and his co-conspirators for brute-forcing SSH servers.

tools.name: Snowflake
tools.description: The Snowflake cloud data platform was exploited by the attackers using stolen credentials to access and exfiltrate large amounts of sensitive data.

vulnerabilities.name: Snowflake Data Breaches 2024
vulnerabilities.description: Weaknesses related to the Snowflake cloud data platform, primarily involving the use of stolen customer credentials without multi-factor authentication, were exploited to gain access to sensitive data as part of a series of major breaches in 2024.

identities.name: Cameron John Wagenius
identities.description: A 22-year-old former U.S. Army soldier sentenced to 70 months in federal prison for orchestrating a hacking and extortion campaign under the alias 'kiberphant0m'.

identities.name: AT&T
identities.description: A major U.S. telecommunications provider targeted by 'kiberphant0m', from which sensitive customer and business data was stolen.

identities.name: Verizon
identities.description: A major U.S. telecommunications company mentioned as a victim of the hacking and extortion campaign.

identities.name: U.S. Army
identities.description: The employer of Cameron John Wagenius during his cybercrime campaign. His actions were described as a form of insider threat to the military.

infrastructure.name: BreachForums
infrastructure.description: A notorious cybercrime forum where 'kiberphant0m' threatened to leak stolen data if the ransom was not paid.

infrastructure.name: XSS.is
infrastructure.description: A cybercrime forum where 'kiberphant0m' threatened to leak stolen data if the ransom was not paid.

indicators.name: SSH Brute-Force Login Attempts
indicators.pattern:
title: SSH Brute-Force Login Attempts
id: 2b8c1f9a-5d7e-4b0f-8c1d-9e8a7b6c5d4e
status: experimental
description: Detects a high volume of failed SSH login attempts, which could be indicative of a brute-force attack like the one conducted using the 'SSH Brute' tool. This is a weak signal and requires aggregation by a SIEM to be effective.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-28
references:
  - https://therecord.media/hacker-telecom-army-sentenced
level: medium
tags:
  - attack.t1110.001
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: sshd
detection:
  keywords:
    - 'Failed password for'
    - 'authentication failure for'
  condition: keywords
indicators.description: Detects failed SSH login attempts. A high volume from a single source IP may indicate a brute-force attack similar to the one described in the article.
